newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: WTO praises Zambia's economic reforms.
newsitem.headline: WTO praises Zambia's economic reforms.

text.p: Zambia is starting to reap the benefits of economic and trade reforms, enjoying lower inflation and a doubling of non-traditional manufactured exports since 1991, the World Trade Organisation (WTO) said on Tuesday.

The global watchdog, in its first review of Zambia's trade policies, said the government had decontrolled prices, privatised many state-owned companies and lifted exchange controls on its currency, the kwacha.

"Zambia's adjustment effort is beginning to show signs of success. In particular its non-traditional exports have grown rapidly and are starting to lead a diversification of the economy away from its dependence on copper," the WTO said.

Zambia is among the world's top five countries in terms of copper reserves, refining capacity and production. Copper exports account for more than 70 per cent of foreign exchange earnings, while cobalt exports make up a further 10 per cent.
Siamukayumbu Siamujaye, Zambian Minister for Commerce, Trade and Industry, attended a two-day meeting at the 123-member state WTO which was to wind up discussion of the report on Tuesday.
Zambia's Privatisation Agency, set up in 1992, has privatised 138 state-owned companies, according to Siamujaye.

"My government's commitment to privatisation remains unshaken as demonstrated by the fact that even strategic companies like ZCCM are due for sale," he said in a speech, referring to Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines.

The WTO said nearly all state-owned companies have been privatised, with the exception of Zambia's Electrical Supply Corporation, its telecommunications sector and the Zambian National Oil Company which still exercise monopoly rights.
Inflation has dropped from more than 100 per cent in 1992 and 1993 to nearly 35 per cent last year, according to WTO.
Non-traditional exports, mainly from the manufacturing sector, have doubled in the past four years and grew by about 35 per cent in 1995, it added.
